companies.note: Plans, builds and hands over wind and solar parks to funds, energy suppliers, Stadtwerke and infrastructure investors; a sister company runs them afterwards. Owner-managed.

Develops, finances, builds and operates wind and solar parks; keeps a large own portfolio and sells single parks and portfolios to investors. Uses project finance and has also raised corporate debt (promissory note loan).

50/50 joint venture of the Aloys Wobben Stiftung (owner of Enercon) and EWE, since 2021. Keeps its parks: more than 2.5 GW in its own portfolio in Germany, France and Greece; target up to 5 GW by 2030. Unsecured corporate credit facility raised to €350m (Dec 2025).

Investment platform backed by its Q-Energy funds. Grew in Germany by buying developers and pipelines: DunoAir's business (2023), a 250 MW portfolio (Jan 2025), several repowering pipelines (2025) and 91 MW from PNE (Jan 2026).

One of Germany's largest solar IPPs (about 3.8 GW in operation, 1.5 GW under construction). Financed with project-finance frameworks (e.g. €216m senior secured from LBBW, Mar 2025) and mezzanine debt. Filed for insolvency in Sept 2026 after a key financing for solar-plus-storage projects failed; parks keep running, an asset sale is under way.

Develops and sells wind, solar and storage projects in many countries. Expected a 2025 loss of about €170m; signed a standstill agreement with its banks in Jan 2026 and is restructuring (project sales, bond waiver).
Restructuring since the parent BayWa's 2024 crisis: a planned stake sale to EIP fell through; the company refocuses on development plus its own power portfolio and has left Asia-Pacific.

events.issue: Turbine maker (formerly REpower) filed for insolvency after losses and delays; it stopped making onshore turbines. Its share of new German turbines fell to zero.
Quality problems with the 4.X and 5.X onshore platforms; sales were restricted in 2023 and restarted in Europe from late 2024.
Parent BayWa's debt crisis; stake sale to EIP failed; asset sales and retreat from Asia-Pacific.
Expected 2025 loss of about €170m; standstill agreement with banks and bondholders; restructuring officer appointed.
Illiquidity and over-indebtedness. The CEO cited oversubscribed onshore tenders that pushed prices down, with most awards going to the north and squeezing margins of southern German projects.
Filed at Hamburg court after a key financing for solar-plus-storage projects failed; reported debt about €3bn. Parks keep running; asset sale with more than 100 interested investors.

notes: Nordex: about 32 % of new onshore capacity in Germany in 2025 (1,647 MW).
